title: Dual tracers permit a 0.74-5.64 year mean-age rise on A20 sigma0 26.5 in 2012-2021 with a 50-year age limit and 2% tolerance
abstract: We tested whether the 2012-2021 oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 at 52 W requires a change in oxygen use at fixed age. We used paired CFC-12 and SF6 in GLODAPv2.2023 and linear programs over all age spectra, with no fixed spectrum shape. An exact history-knot reduction preserves both tracers and mean age. For six matched A20 latitude bins, AOU rose by 18.32 umol/kg. With a 50-year age limit and 2% tracer tolerance, the allowed mean-age rise was 0.74-5.64 years. This range contains the 3.87 years needed to account for the mean AOU gain at a rate of 4.73 umol/kg/year. At 5% tolerance the age-change range was -1.82 to 7.74 years. Level tests were stricter: a constant rate of 4.73 and zero preformed AOU fitted both years in only four of six A20 bins, or three with a component-oxygen floor of 100 umol/kg. No tested common rate and preformed-AOU pair fitted all A20 bins. A22 allowed complete fits at other parameter values. Thus a small fitted inverse-Gaussian age change does not bound the mean-age change, but a full ventilation-only explanation of A20 is not established. Bounds depend on source saturation, the partial-pressure mixing approximation, tail support and tolerance. Code, aggregate results, provenance and independent audits are included. External records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Allowed mean-age change ranges at 5% tracer tolerance. These are feasible-set bounds, not confidence intervals.
Matched bins with constant-rate fits to both tracer and AOU levels, at 5% tolerance. Counts show failed cases as well as fits.

citations.reason: The small inverse-Gaussian age change is not a shape-free bound on mean-age change. Our level tests do not establish a complete ventilation-only explanation.
